class ara::core::BasicString

[SWS_CORE_03000]

User Guide AI generated

Automatically generated description, content derived from the referenced AUTOSAR R25-11 specification elements — not an official AUTOSAR text. Evidence: [SWS_…] references.

intended use

ara::core::BasicString<Allocator> implements std::pmr::basic_string and parameterizes the allocation via Allocator [SWS_CORE_03000] [SWS_CORE_03005]. It provides capacity management, iterators, element access, and append, insert, replace, compare, and search operations [SWS_CORE_03054] [SWS_CORE_03077] [SWS_CORE_03094] [SWS_CORE_03110] [SWS_CORE_03346] [SWS_CORE_03315].

Generation & destruction

The type can be empty, created from an allocator, a string, a character range, an initializer list, or a StringView [SWS_CORE_03024] [SWS_CORE_03025] [SWS_CORE_03028] [SWS_CORE_03031] [SWS_CORE_03302]. Copy construction and copy assignment are available; Move construction is noexcept while move assignment depends on allocator properties [SWS_CORE_03020] [SWS_CORE_03021] [SWS_CORE_03022] [SWS_CORE_03023].

Lifecycle & Ownership

The object owns its characters and returns the allocator used via get_allocator() [SWS_CORE_03415]. c_str(), data() and the conversion to StringView allow access to the character representation [SWS_CORE_03069] [SWS_CORE_03070] [SWS_CORE_03301].

Interaction with other classes

StringView is accepted in constructors as well as in append, insert, replace, compare, assign and search operations [SWS_CORE_03302] [SWS_CORE_03308] [SWS_CORE_03310] [SWS_CORE_03312] [SWS_CORE_03321] [SWS_CORE_03087] [SWS_CORE_03315].

Limitations & Error handling

For position errors, at() and several modification and substring operations use IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation; size overruns in reserve(), resize(), append(), insert(), or assign() use IsoStdLengthErrorViolation instead of the respective standard exception [SWS_CORE_03064] [SWS_CORE_03054] [SWS_CORE_03059] [SWS_CORE_03078] [SWS_CORE_03095] [SWS_CORE_03088]. Many mutating operations are not exception-safe [SWS_CORE_03077] [SWS_CORE_03104] [SWS_CORE_03110].

Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                              function assign [SWS_CORE_03086]
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              BasicString & assign (const BasicString &str, size_type pos, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if (pos > str.size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                              Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                              The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::assign (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::out_of_range, the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if (pos > str.size())”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                      function assign [SWS_CORE_03088]
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      BasicString & assign (const value_type *s, size_type n);
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( n > max_size() ) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std:: length_error
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                      Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                      The behavior of this element is not specified independently, but is defined by reference to ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; the relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::assign (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from std semantics according to the specification: adaptation of the signature to ara types (“charT replaced with value_type”); instead of std::length_error, the Violation IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised (condition according to the specification: “if ( n > max_size() )”). Unlike a catchable std exception, a Violation is not recoverable: it constitutes a violated precondition/postcondition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and causes abnormal process termination through Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                          template <class T> BasicString & assign (const T &t, size_type pos, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if (pos > sv.size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                          Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                          Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                          The behavior of this element is not specified independently in the specification, but is defined through the reference to ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; the corresponding counterpart is std::basic_string::assign (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::out_of_range, violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised (condition according to the specification: “if (pos > sv.size())”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation cannot be handled: it is considered a violated precondition/postcondition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination through Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]). The record is marked DRAFT in SWS Core; its content is therefore not yet binding.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function copy [SWS_CORE_03410]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              size_type copy (value_type *s, size_type n, size_type pos=0) const;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos > size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::copy (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: Signature adaptation to ara types (“charT replaced with value_type”); instead of std::out_of_range the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos > size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function erase [SWS_CORE_03102]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              BasicString & erase (size_type pos=0, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos > size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::erase (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: Signature adaptation to ara types (“charT replaced with value_type”); instead of std::out_of_range the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos > size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function insert [SWS_CORE_03094]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              BasicString & insert (size_type pos1, const BasicString &str, size_type pos2, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > str.size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::insert (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::out_of_range the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > str.size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos1 > size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range 3. if ( size() + n > max_size() ) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std::length_error
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::insert (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: Signature adaptation to ara types (“charT replaced with value_type”); instead of std::out_of_range the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos1 > size() )”); instead of std::length_error the violation IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( size() + n > max_size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).



                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function insert [SWS_CORE_03311]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  template <class T> BasicString & insert (size_type pos1, const T &t, size_type pos2, size_type n=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > sv.size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::insert (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::out_of_range, the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > sv.size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]). The record is marked in the SWS Core as DRAFT, the content is therefore not yet binding.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function replace [SWS_CORE_03107]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              BasicString & replace (size_type pos1, size_type n1, const BasicString &str, size_type pos2, size_type n2=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos > max_size() || pos2 > str.size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::replace (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: Signature adaptation to ara types (“charT replaced with value_type”); instead of std::out_of_range the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos > max_size() || pos2 > str.size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function replace [SWS_CORE_03108]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  BasicString & replace (size_type pos, size_type n1, const value_type *s, size_type n2);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos1 > size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range 3. IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std::length_error (see condition in [11] )
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Bibliography SWS Core: [11] ISO/IEC 14882:2017, Programming languages – C++ – www.iso.org
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The behavior of this element is not specified independently, but is defined by the reference to ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; the relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::replace (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from std semantics according to the specification: signature adaptation to ara types ("charT replaced with value_type"); instead of std::out_of_range, violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised (condition according to the specification: "if ( pos1 > size() )"); instead of std::length_error, violation IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised. Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation cannot be handled: it is considered a violated precondition/postcondition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and causes abnormal process termination through Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          template <class T> BasicString & replace (size_type pos1, size_type n1, const T &t, size_type pos2, size_type n2=npos);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > sv.size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::replace (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: Signature adaptation to ara types (“charT replaced with value_type”); instead of std::out_of_range the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos1 > size() || pos2 > sv.size() )”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]). The record is marked as DRAFT in the SWS Core, so the content is not yet binding.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  void reserve (size_type res_arg=0);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if (res_arg > max_size()) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std:: length_error
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The behavior of this element is not specified independently, but is defined by reference to ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; the relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::reserve (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::length_error, the Violation IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised (condition according to the specification: “if (res_arg > max_size())”). Unlike a catchable std exception, a Violation is not recoverable: it constitutes a violated precondition/postcondition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and causes abnormal process termination through Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).

                                                                                                                                                                                     

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function substr [SWS_CORE_03345]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          BasicString substr (size_type pos=0, size_type n=npos) const;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. if ( pos > size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The behavior of this element is not specified independently, but is defined by reference to ISO C++ standard section [basic.string]; the relevant counterpart is std::basic_string::substr (cppreference: std::basic_string). Deviations from std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::out_of_range, the Violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised (condition according to the specification: “if ( pos > size() )”). Unlike a catchable std exception, a Violation is not recoverable: it constitutes a violated precondition/postcondition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and causes abnormal process termination through Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]).
